solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lovely being by isle

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
I is the standard abbreviation for isle or island

explanation.surface: Someone admires a beautiful creature beside an island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a beautiful fairy or elf-like spirit.

clue.text: Trouble at a hostel in Scots council area

indicators.note: trouble as a verb means disturb, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: There is a disturbance at a youth hostel in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' rearranges AT A HOSTEL IN.
explanation.definitionFit: East Lothian is a Scottish local authority east of Edinburgh.

clue.text: Dull elderly relative boring two friends endlessly

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the relative goes inside the two

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
nan is a grandmother

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for friends loses its last letter

parts.note: mates are friends

explanation.surface: An old relative tediously pesters a couple of pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like the definition beside 'Dull', but signals drilling in; 'endlessly' drops a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, without spirit, hence dull.

clue.text: Eating al fresco, taking photos?

parts.note: a pic is a photo, short for picture
nicking is British slang for stealing or taking

explanation.surface: Diners eating outdoors are busy snapping pictures of their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'taking photos' backwards as nicking pics, then put the pieces in answer order; the question mark flags the jokey re-reading of picnicking as pic-nicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is an outdoor meal, so having one is eating in the open air.

clue.text: Go with raised hire charge

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the whole run is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rent is to hire
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a higher rental fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RENTRAP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To partner someone is to accompany them, as a dance partner does.

clue.text: Pass soldiers: trouble quickly starts in resort

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
ado means fuss, trouble
springs means leaps up, starts quickly

explanation.surface: Troops crossing a mountain pass run into trouble at a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a US city long known as a health spa and holiday destination.

clue.text: Russian leaving capital of SW Europe

indicators.note: leaving capital means the word for Russian drops its capital, its initial letter

parts.note: a Siberian is a Russian from Siberia

explanation.surface: A Russian departs from a city in southern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian describes the peninsula of Spain and Portugal in the south-west of the continent.

clue.text: Goddess in hearts of Miro and Genet

indicators.note: hearts of means the inner letters of each named artist and writer

explanation.surface: A goddess at the centre of works by a Spanish painter and a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Miró was a Spanish painter and Genet a French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene (Eirene) was the Greek goddess of peace.

clue.text: Author's Little Greek Donkey

parts.note: little means short, and Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A writer has a small Greek donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass was the German novelist who wrote The Tin Drum.

clue.text: Drug runner in suit cut for shoe

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: in places the runner inside the trimmed card suit
cut means the suit name loses its last letter

parts.note: spades is one of the four card suits
a rill is a small stream, something that runs

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler is found wearing a tailored suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete or drug mule, but here it is a stream; 'in' and 'cut' do the building.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

clue.text: Rock knocked over a giant

indicators.note: knocked over in a crossing clue means the word for rock is turned backwards

parts.note: a gem is a rock in slang, as a diamond is a 'rock'

explanation.surface: A huge boulder is toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns GEM into MEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega as an adjective means huge, enormous.

clue.text: American cat penning book in Britain

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the book letter sits inside the American cat

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A US big cat writes a book while living in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is an old poetic name for Britain or England.

clue.text: One entering lists makes merry

indicators.note: entering means the numeral for one goes inside the lists

parts.note: rosters are lists of duty names
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone joining the duty rotas is having a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily, to revel.

clue.text: Orator right in it with Horace unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately means the letters of it and Horace end up badly arranged

explanation.surface: A public speaker is wrongly lumped in with the Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here; 'unfortunately' scrambles the name of the Roman poet Horace with 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorician is an expert in the art of persuasive speaking.

clue.text: Trimmed ermine covered colonnade

indicators.note: trimmed means the animal's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: An ermine-trimmed garment hangs in a covered walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a roofed portico of ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Fish head added to Greek dish regularly

indicators.note: added to means the head word follows the picked letters
regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: napper is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A fish head is tossed into a Greek dish now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'Greek dish' to give REDS; NAPPER, old slang for the head, is then added on.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper is a reddish food fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Courtesy from constables arresting drunken earl

indicators.note: arresting means the constables hold the drunk earl inside

parts.note: a posse is a body of constables summoned by a sheriff
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Police politely detain a drunk aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is formal politeness, from the French.

clue.text: Sex toys Dane abused in shocking film

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: abused means the letters of toys and Dane are mistreated into a new order

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of a Danish man misusing adult toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' looks like part of the lurid surface, but is Latin for six; 'abused' gives the anagram, which follows the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Video nasty was the British tabloid term for a violent or gory horror film on tape.

clue.text: Somebody illustrious accepting thanks

indicators.note: accepting means the noble word takes the thanks inside it

parts.note: noble means grand, illustrious
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A famous person graciously receives gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somebody illustrious' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Somebody', a person of note.
explanation.definitionFit: A somebody is a person of importance, a notable or celebrity.

clue.text: About to quell resistance in the old city

indicators.note: in places the shortened about word inside the old form of the

parts.note: ye is an old way of writing the

indicators.note: to quell means to suppress, so the resistance letter is put down and removed

parts.note: around means about
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Something is about to crush opposition in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' is fodder and 'to quell' the deletion; 'the old' is a standard archaism.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital of Cameroon.

clue.text: See work doubling in line?

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to look at work being duplicated in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a line or cord that curves back on itself, a doubled-over stretch.

clue.text: Doctor cares not for predecessor

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A GP is indifferent to the patient who came before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges CARES NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear, one who came before in a family line.

clue.text: Extensive article leads to more advanced state

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, and leads to says it comes first
long means extensive

explanation.surface: A lengthy newspaper feature brings about progress.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words appear back to front: the article leads, so it goes before the word for extensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Along means forward, onward in progress, as in 'coming along nicely'.

clue.text: Inflation-affected company's capital?

indicators.note: affected here means the company is pumped up, with the air put inside it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
inflation is done with air

explanation.surface: A firm's capital has been hit by rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial, beside 'Inflation' and 'company'; it is a capital city, Egypt's.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Get the better of fool backing Oxford University

indicators.note: backing means the fool word sits behind, supporting the university letters

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: Outsmarting an idiot who supports Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit is to outsmart, to beat by cleverness.

clue.text: Shedding wings, I will be pagan deity

indicators.note: shedding wings means the element's name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A creature loses its wings and is reborn as a heathen god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker; it is the symbol of iodine, and 'Shedding wings' strips its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, worshipped by pre-Christian Scandinavians.

clue.text: Unhinged family in Peel

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, unhinged
kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A mad family living in a place called Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' looks like a place name (there is one on the Isle of Man) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit's skin is its peel, the classic slapstick slipping hazard.

clue.text: I'm surprised don seems unsettled on leave

indicators.note: on means the anagram is placed after the verb for leave

parts.note: go means leave, depart

indicators.note: unsettled means the letters of don seems are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An academic looks uneasy about being given time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like an academic, but is just fodder for 'unsettled'; 'on' puts the verb first.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodness me is an exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: Second bird observed in winter nest?

indicators.note: observed in means the letters can be seen running inside winter nest

explanation.surface: Another bird is spotted in a nest in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Both TERN and this bird sit inside 'winter nest'; 'Second' picks the later one.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large bird of prey.
